blocks.text: The clone asked to come. He asked as Nuria had: standing, without an altar, accepting the no if the no came. Andrés didn't refuse him. Lía set only one condition: she would be beside the circle, and she would ask him the question before anyone embraced him, so that the embrace wouldn't sign in advance what still had to be known.

blocks.text: Aya made the coffee, two cups, the cracked one and the one that had crossed, and let them cool for half a minute, and warmed them again, because the time of the assembling won't be ruled by a clock, not even by the one that ran two minutes slow.

blocks.text: The hangar, far away, fell into a dense silence. Andrés, in the warehouse at El Estacio, felt through the bridge the beginning of the hollow (the dissolving, the cold) and then the bridge was cut, as it had been cut with Nuria. For the first time since the ship had left, the sky stopped writing. The chair on the shore, and the chair of the one who searches, were left at the mercy of a name that travelled without being a place.

blocks.text: To Aya, the while felt longer than the levante. She didn't notify Madrid. She looked at the circle. Lía, motionless, had her wrist alight, and not in order to heal.

blocks.text: Then there was a weight. There was a young man, strong, with Andrés's face from another time, rope-worker's hands that work had not yet marked, dark and patient eyes. He breathed. He asked for air, like Nuria. He saw Lía first, and Aya, and the Andrés of the shore, older in his features, halted at the age Lía had closed for him, and he said neither “father” nor “son”. He said, in a voice that was this house's voice and wasn't:

blocks.text: “I've crossed. Am I still me?”
blocks.html: “I've crossed. Am I still me?”

blocks.text: Lía didn't embrace him yet.
blocks.html: Lía didn't embrace him yet.

blocks.text: “If you both remember the same storm, which of you is my father?”
blocks.html: “If you both remember the same storm, which of you is my father?”

blocks.text: The young man smiled, and the one from the shore smiled with him, and the coincidence hurt them and was enough for them.
blocks.html: The young man smiled, and the one from the shore smiled with him, and the coincidence hurt them and was enough for them.

blocks.text: “Both of us,” said the one who had just been put together, just as on the night of the ship. “One to stay and one to search. I've searched, and now I've come. The hollow exists. I'm telling you because you asked her, Nuria, and it was true. An instant when I belonged nowhere. Then I saw you, and I knew the name of this light, and your mother's name, and his. If I'm missing something I can't name, you'll tell me, if you see it.”

blocks.text: Then Lía took his hand, with permission, and looked inside. She saw the text of a cloned body, an artificial brain, the memories of the shore and of the worlds, the sowings, the letters, and a new layer, the layer of the hollow, brief and dark, like a silence between two sentences. She didn't amend it. She let go of his hand and, at last, embraced him, and then embraced the one from the shore, and the two smells mingled for her: the salt of home and the smell of newly ordered metal.

blocks.text: Aya came closer more slowly. She touched the face of the one who had arrived with a threshold attentiveness, the same with which she had once measured three tenths of a second before a boat growing smaller.

blocks.text: “You're you, and you're not the one from this chair,” she said. “I waited for you at a departure. Now I'm waiting for you at an arrival. There's coffee. It's in both cups. Choose, or don't choose, and sit down.”

blocks.text: Later they sat, not in the warehouse but in the courtyard in Lo Pagán, the four of them, plus Iago for a while, who brought figs and asked for no doctrine. The Mar Menor was flat as a plate. The one who had crossed looked at it the way you look at a relative you owe a visit to, not at a portrait. He said the water, seen like this, was smaller than in memory and more sufficient. Andrés, the one from the shore, laughed quietly, because that was what he had felt with the other sea: what is your own, in the end, fits in a glass, and is enough.

blocks.text: They talked little about the machines. They talked about the garden, the white strand of hair, Vicente, a Nuria who had gone back to her hangar with a taste in her mouth. The one who searches didn't stay to live. He couldn't: his trade was searching, and this shore, though it called him, was no longer his only place. He stayed, like Nuria, a few days. He slept in the room that had been Lía's as a girl, or on a blanket in the courtyard, when the air allowed. In the mornings the two Andréses went out, not always together: one to the boat, the other to walk the promenade, and the people, who had already seen everything, still paused a little on seeing them, the way you pause before a mirror that walks.

blocks.text: One afternoon, facing the water, the one from the shore asked the one who had crossed:
blocks.html: One afternoon, facing the water, the one from the shore asked the one who had crossed:

blocks.text: “Are you the same one who left in the ship?”
blocks.html: “Are you the same one who left in the ship?”

blocks.text: The other took his time.
blocks.html: The other took his time.

blocks.text: “I'm the one who remembers leaving, and the one who remembers a hollow, and the one who's here. If that's the same, then yes. If being the same requires never having been interrupted, I don't know. Lía is right: an order can be exact and, even so, there can have been a while when there was nobody. I'm not asking you to settle it. I'm asking you to let me go back to searching, and to come back, sometimes, through this circle, if you keep a coffee for me.”

blocks.text: “We'll keep it for you,” said Andrés.

blocks.text: Aya, from the doorstep, watched the two of them, and didn't have to choose which was the man of the house. That week, the house stretched to two weights, two voices, a single afternoon snack. In the chip, Eva asked, softly:

blocks.text: *If two men remember the same storm and one has passed through a hollow, is the storm still one, or are there two now, with a silence between them? And if the daughter embraces them both, isn't that an answer, or is it only a while, which doesn't travel?*

blocks.text: MAY, the fact:
blocks.html: MAY, the fact:

blocks.text: *The one who searches was taken apart in a hangar and put together at El Estacio. He asked for air. He answered “both of us”. He slept on this shore for a few days. The bridge of the letters was cut during the hollow and afterwards wasn't needed, because both were in the same courtyard. That is the fact.*

blocks.text: When the one who searches stepped into the circle again, to leave once more for a world that didn't yet have a name, Andrés didn't hold him back. They stood for a second with their foreheads almost touching, and Lía said the three names, the mooring: Andrés, Andrés, Lía. Aya added her own, so that the edge would stay where it belonged. Then a dense silence, a lighter chair, and, after a while, a short letter from a hangar: “I've arrived. I'm still, if I am, the one who searches. Keep my coffee for me.”

blocks.text: They kept it. That night the one from the shore slept on his own ground, with Aya beside him, and dreamed not of the valley of faces but of a courtyard with two cups and still water, and that, after a reunion, was a way of not getting lost, and also of letting go.
